title: Mini SDK Accelerator — Quicklaunch Templates & Opinionated Playflow
content:
Purpose:
This doc is an opinionated, minimal "mini-course" and quicklaunch kit for internal SDK teams and solutions engineers to run a 30–90 minute onboarding session with customers or internal integrators. It intentionally trades breadth for repeatable outcomes: a single-file starter app, an automated smoke harness, and a short checklist to validate production readiness for basic integration patterns.

Goals (what a 30–90 minute run should achieve):
- Developer has a working hello-world integration calling Redwood API (text generation + streaming) in <= 20 minutes.
- Basic telemetry (request id, latency, token usage) emits to our sandbox telemetry endpoint.
- Integration includes one failure-mode fallback: short-circuit to a cached response or smaller model.
- CI smoke test runs automatically on PR and validates samples.

Audience:
- Developer advocates and solutions engineers running demos
- Small engineering teams doing first integration with Redwood SDKs
- Internal bootcamps for new SDK maintainers

Constraints / Opinionated tradeoffs (short list):
- Minimal dependencies: use a single language binding (JS/TS or Python) per kit, no extra frameworks.
- Single entrypoint: starter is one file (app.js / starter.py) plus a README and .env.example.
- No long-running infra: all examples call Hosted API; Dedicated/private-specific notes are in an appendix.
- Latency-first defaults: encourage streaming, connection keep-alive, small request timeouts (3s for first token).

Course flow (30-min fast path, expandable to 90):
Module 0 — Prep (5 min)
- Ensure user has API key and sandbox org
- Clone starter repo and open file
- Confirm node/Python version using nvm/pyenv snippet

Module 1 — Hello call (10 min)
- Walk through starter file: ENV, small helper, call to RedwoodAPI.generate or client.chat.stream
- Run: `node starter.js` or `python starter.py`
- Verify streaming output and request id printed to console

Module 2 — Telemetry & Observability (5–10 min)
- Explain telemetry contract: request_id, model, region, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, sdk_version
- Quick toggle in starter to send telemetry to sandbox endpoint and show JSON payload example

Module 3 — Failure mode & Fallback (5–10 min)
- Simulate rate limit or model OOM by flipping an env var (SIMULATE_RATE_LIMIT=true)
- Starter falls back to: a) local cached answer for common prompts, b) a smaller compatible model (e.g., redwood-small-instruct)
- Show sample logs and how the SDK surfaces fallback decisions

Module 4 — CI smoke & PR gating (10–15 min)
- Add tiny GH Action / CircleCI job: run smoke harness that executes 3 sample prompts and asserts expected tokens < 100 and HTTP 200
- Explain how this prevents accidental regressions when upgrading SDK or changing defaults

Quickstart files (example content snippets):
- README (starter): short checklist + run commands
- .env.example:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx
  REDWOOD_ENV=sandbox
  TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT=https://telemetry-sandbox.redwood.com/ingest
  SIMULATE_RATE_LIMIT=false
- starter.js (JS sample skeleton):
  const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  async function main(){
    try{
      const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages: [{role:'user', content:'Hello'}] });
      for await (const chunk of stream){ process.stdout.write(chunk.text); }
    } catch(e){
      console.error('call failed', e.message);
      // fallback: load cached or call smaller model
    }
  }
  main();

- starter.py (Python minimal): similar flow using `redwood.Client` and `.stream_chat()` with a small generator to print tokens

Telemetry contract (example JSON emitted):
{
  "request_id": "req_abc123",
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "latency_ms": 128,
  "tokens_in": 23,
  "tokens_out": 67,
  "sdk_version": "0.18.0"
}

Smoke harness checks (text assertions):
- Response contains greeting tokens and ends with newline
- tokens_out < 200 for the sample prompt
- No HTTP 5xx returned

Failure-mode matrix (compact):
- Condition: rate_limit -> Observable: 429 with Retry-After -> Action: backoff (jitter), if persistent -> fallback to cached answer or smaller model.
- Condition: model_oom -> Observable: 500 with oom tag -> Action: call compatible quantized model, mark trace with oom=true.
- Condition: network_partition -> Observable: connection timeout -> Action: return friendly error, enqueue telemetry for postmortem.

Ops notes for Solutions Engineers:
- Recommended defaults for demo envs: streaming enabled, keepalive true, timeout 30s global but 3s for first token heuristic.
- Recommended sample prompts to surface token usage and safety: short greeting, concise summarization, and one open question causing longer output.
- Add `--record` flag to local runner to save the request/response pair for post-demo analysis.

Appendix A — One-page README template (to drop into starter repo):
- Title: Redwood mini-sdk quicklaunch
- Objective: Run a hello-world call to Redwood API and observe telemetry + fallback
- Steps: 1) copy .env.example to .env and set API key; 2) `npm install` or `pip install -r requirements.txt`; 3) `npm run start` or `python starter.py`; 4) view telemetry at sandbox UI; 5) open PR to add a new sample prompt (CI will run smoke tests).

Appendix B — Open questions / TODO (team action items):
- Decide canonical language set for the mini kit: JS, Python, Go? start with JS+Python now.
- Centralize telemetry ingestion endpoint for demo accounts vs. prod — who owns retention? (ask observability team)
- Create a small set of curated sample prompts that demonstrate cost/regression scenarios across models
- Add a tiny UX flow to the Console that maps a sample request id to a recorded PR diff in the sample repo (nice to have).

Appendix C — Troubleshooting cheatsheet (quick commands):
- Validate API key: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health`
- Reproduce streaming locally with verbose logs: `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug node starter.js`
- Force fallback: `SIMULATE_RATE_LIMIT=true node starter.js`

Notes to self (authoring hints):
- Keep examples intentionally small; avoid deep dive into rollout or private deployment nuances inside the primary flow. Those belong in separate appendices for Dedicated/Private SDKs.
- Prefer real request ids in screenshots to help SRE trace logs during demos.

If this flow looks good, next steps: convert to a tiny GH repo template, add GH Action smoke harness, and create a 30-min runbook for Solutions that includes common troubleshooting Slack threads and a single escalation contact.

-- Maya
